claim: the spring return is slower than the extension
at 1 bar it still reaches the end, much more slowly: 1 bar x A = 31.4 N, just above spring 25 N + friction 6 N
measured: x max 50.0 mm, extend 0.266 s vs 0.0272 s

claim: a stiffer spring returns faster
released after 15 ms the piston stops part-way and comes back
a 5 kg tool overshoots into the end stop (rebounds)
a small valve (30 l/min) slows both strokes
measured: extend 0.252 vs 0.087 s, return 0.302 vs 0.0987 s

claim: indirect control starts later than direct control (pilot filling)
a 10 m pilot line starts the cylinder later
pilot needing 4 bar on a 3 bar supply: nothing moves
either station extends the cylinder (two strokes)
overlapping presses give one longer stroke, nothing new
the cylinder starts only when the second hand arrives (1.5 s)
hands that never overlap: no motion
a quarter of the opening (20 % to 5 %): the return takes about four times longer
meter-in is faster at the same settings
a 60 N load slows meter-in far more than meter-out
the quick-exhaust valve shortens the extension (vs L03)
a tap on start keeps it extended after the release; a tap on return brings it back
overlapping signals: still extended at the end
return held until 7.5 s: it returns when start is released at 7 s
